title: Generalizable Knowledge Distillation from Vision Foundation Models for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Two-stage KD from a VFM. Stage 1 distils domain-agnostic features into the student by query-based soft feature distillation. Stage 2 freezes those features and trains the task head, so the student keeps the VFM's out-of-domain robustness.
adaptation: Stage 1: distil DINOv2-L or DINOv3 patch features into the ResNet-34 encoder on the 11.9k pool (or the 159k pool). Stage 2: house training under PF so the distilled encoder is not erased. Target: E1 generalisation.
min_experiment: Arm: GKD-initialised R34 + PF fine-tune, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF from ImageNet. Metrics: E1 crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, clean-49 crack IoU. Kill: E1 metrics within noise of PF and no test gain.
evidence: R: average gains +1.9% (foundation-to-foundation) and +10.6% (foundation-to-local) over prior KD methods on 5 domain-generalisation segmentation benchmarks.
prior_overlap: Partial. The pool feature-learning row (MIM, DDeP on R34) was n.d. VFM feature distillation is a different objective, and BRIEF lists other SSL objectives as open.

alt_notes.adaptation: Student = house R34 encoder; stage 1 feature distillation from DINOv2-L or C-RADIOv4 on the 11.9k pool; stage 2 house training, encoder frozen then PF.
alt_notes.min_experiment: GKD-initialised R34 vs house PF; E1 relF1@2 and E1 inactive IoU; kill if not +0.03 E1 relF1@2.
